title: Add bee worktree prune over the classifier, with dry-run and a reason per worktree
action: Decisions D2 and D5. `bee worktree prune [--dry-run] [--older-than-days N] [--json]`, routed in the try_native match at handlers.rs:661, calling wr-2's classifier and wr-1's teardown helper per dead worktree. Output: ONE line per worktree naming the id and its reason, kept or removed. The removal line names the reclaimed size -- this is the one place size is paid for (D4a) -- and the report names `git worktree lock` as the permanent opt-out, which is enforced by git itself: a locked tree makes `git worktree remove -f` die with 'cannot remove a locked working tree'. --dry-run runs the classifier and removes NOTHING. ENUMERATION: read granted ids AND the entries under .bee/runtime/workspaces/, unioned. A grant-driven scan alone never visits a grantless orphan record, and CONTEXT.md promises one prune run clears the 13 orphans that already exist on this machine. REGISTRY PAYLOAD (D5): the declared regen chain -- `node scripts/export_registry_payload.mjs` per tests/registry_contracts.rs:157 -- does not exist here; scripts/ holds only install.sh and install.ps1 and the repo contains zero .mjs/.js/.ts files. So hand-edit generated/registry_payload.json and record that reason in the cell trace. Two mechanics ride along: the payload is a SINGLE 168KB line, so the edit diffs as one changed line; and registry examples are EXECUTED by tests/registry_dispatch.rs:131 inside a scratch dir that is NOT a git repo, and the first example must not print a refusal marker. Model the example on worktree merge's deliberately inert `--id demo-feature-missing`: prune's example must succeed and do nothing outside a git repo. Add --dry-run to the example.

truths: --dry-run classifies and removes nothing, verified by asserting the directory still exists after the run
A grantless orphan workspace record is reached and dropped
The registry example runs green in registry_dispatch.rs's non-git scratch dir
artifacts: A test for the dry-run no-op and a test for the union enumeration
prohibitions: Do not make the registry example destructive or dependent on a git repo
Do not bypass wr-2's classifier with an inline shortcut for any worktree
Do not touch merge's cleanup default in this cell -- that is wr-4

trace.outcome: Added bee worktree prune over classify_worktree, with dry-run, older-than-days, union enumeration of grants and workspace records, and a hand-edited registry payload entry
